title: metadata-fanout-during-stage-swap-caused-overprovision-and-rollback-latch
creator: Miguel Alvarez
description: During a staged canary swap for model v2026-03-beta, an unexpected metadata duplication in the route reconciliation path caused a fanout of stage-change events across multiple orchestrator partitions. This produced a transient surge in deployment actions that triggered autoscaler overprovisioning and saturated our KV cache sync path. Several rollback attempts became blocked when the controller observed mixed pin states and refused to reconcile until shard-level checkpoints completed, resulting in a ~37 minute partial outage for 4% of requests routed to the affected model family.
timeline: 2026-02-18T09:12Z - Canary swap initiated from console for v2026-03-beta (10% -> 50% target).
2026-02-18T09:14Z - Orchestrator emitted duplicate route-change events due to metadata re-emit in stage-swap handler (detected later).
2026-02-18T09:15Z - Autoscaler reacted to perceived new capacity needs and spun up additional pods; cluster IP churn increased request routing noise.
2026-02-18T09:16Z - KV cache sync queue began backpressure; synchronization latency spiked from ~20ms to ~1.2s.
2026-02-18T09:35Z - First manual rollback attempted from Console; controller refused rollback because mixed version pin persisted on 3 of 5 shards.
2026-02-18T09:49Z - Secondary rollback executed with forced-unpin flag by on-call; partial recovery began but route convergence took until 09:56Z.
2026-02-18T09:50Z - Incident declared; on-call paged SRE and rollout-safety engineering.
2026-02-18T10:25Z - Traffic normalized; post-incident monitoring window opened.
2026-02-18T11:00Z - Full post-incident capture exported to S3 (s3://redwood-postmortems/ENG-55111/).
impact_summary: 37 minutes of partial degradation for 4% of online text-generation requests for the model family 'redwood-llama-extended'.
Increased  p95 latency by ~220ms for affected requests during the KV sync backpressure window.
No customer data loss or model state corruption observed; logs and traces were intact for investigation.
root_cause: A bug in the stage-swap metadata handler re-emitted route-change metadata to multiple orchestrator partitions when a swap involved simultaneous variant annotations. The duplicate emits doubled reconciliation work and caused out-of-order version pin updates on some shards. The controller's safety checks treat mixed pin states as non-idempotent and refused automated rollback until shard checkpoints were reconciled, which was gated by the saturated KV sync path.
mitigation: Immediate: Disabled parallel stage annotation propagation in the controller and applied a hotfix to de-duplicate metadata emits (PR #12874).
Immediate: Added a temporary throttle to orchestrator reconciliation loops to prevent autoscaler triggering on transient events.
Short-term: Increased KV sync worker pool and added backpressure metrics to alert earlier when queue depth exceeds safe thresholds.
Long-term: Implement stronger idempotency in version pin updates and introduce a quorum-based fast-unpin path for emergency rollbacks.

followup_notes: We should treat any multi-partition metadata emit as a throttled operation by default; single-request semantics should be enforced at the controller edge.
Autoscaler thresholds were sensitive to short-lived reconciliation churn; we need to decouple autoscaler signals from reconciliation noise signals by introducing a reconciliation cool-down metric.
Consider adding a synthetic canary that validates rollback and unpin paths as part of every staged promotion pipeline to detect blockers before human-triggered rollbacks are needed.
Coordinate with Console team to add a clearer failed-rollback reason in UI so on-call can decide whether to force-unpin or wait for shard convergence.
